sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evaṃ te samayaṃ kṛtvā nyavasaṃs tatra pāṇḍavāḥ vaśe śastrapratāpena kurvanto 'nyān mahīkṣitaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having thus made their compact, the Pāṇḍavas dwelt there, bringing other rulers of the earth under their sway through the might of their weapons.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ manujasiṃhānāṃ pañcānām amitaujasām babhūva kṛṣṇā sarveṣāṃ pārthānāṃ vaśavartinī
english: Kṛṣṇā became obedient to all of those five sons of Pṛthā, those lions among men of immeasurable might.

sanskrit: te tayā taiś ca sā vīraiḥ patibhiḥ saha pañcabhiḥ babhūva paramaprītā nāgair iva sarasvatī
english: And she, together with those five heroic husbands, was supremely content, like the Sarasvatī amid its elephants.

sanskrit: vartamāneṣu dharmeṇa pāṇḍaveṣu mahātmasu vyavardhan kuravaḥ sarve hīnadoṣāḥ sukhānvitāḥ
english: While the great-souled Pāṇḍavas conducted themselves righteously, all the Kurus thrived, free from fault and full of happiness.

sanskrit: atha dīrgheṇa kālena brāhmaṇasya viśāṃ pate kasya cit taskarāḥ ke cij jahrur gā nṛpasattama
english: Then, O lord of the people, O best of kings, after a long time, some thieves stole the cattle of a certain brahmin.

sanskrit: hriyamāṇe dhane tasmin brāhmaṇaḥ krodhamūrcchitaḥ āgamya khāṇḍavaprastham udakrośata pāṇḍavān
english: As his wealth was being carried off, the brahmin, swooning with rage, came to Khāṇḍavaprastha and cried out loudly to the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: hriyate godhanaṃ kṣudrair nṛśaṃsair akṛtātmabhiḥ prasahya vo 'smād viṣayād abhidhāvata pāṇḍavāḥ
english: "My cattle are being carried off by base, cruel, and uncontrolled wretches! Rush out from your domain and pursue them, O Pāṇḍavas!"

sanskrit: brāhmaṇasya pramattasya havir dhvāṅkṣair vilupyate śārdūlasya guhāṃ śūnyāṃ nīcaḥ kroṣṭābhimarśati
english: "The oblation of the heedless brahmin is plundered by crows; a jackal invades the empty cave of the tiger."

sanskrit: brāhmaṇasve hṛte corair dharmārthe ca vilopite rorūyamāṇe ca mayi kriyatām astradhāraṇam
english: "While a brahmin's property is stolen by thieves, while the purpose of righteousness is violated, while I weep aloud — let your weapons be taken up!"

sanskrit: rorūyamāṇasyābhyāśe tasya viprasya pāṇḍavaḥ tāni vākyāni śuśrāva kuntīputro dhanaṃjayaḥ
english: The Pāṇḍava, Dhanañjaya, son of Kuntī, heard those words of the weeping brahmin close by.

sanskrit: śrutvā caiva mahābāhur mā bhair ity āha taṃ dvijam āyudhāni ca yatrāsan pāṇḍavānāṃ mahātmanām kṛṣṇayā saha tatrāsīd dharmarājo yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: Hearing this, the mighty-armed one said to the brahmin, "Fear not." But where the weapons of the great-souled Pāṇḍavas were kept, King Yudhiṣṭhira the dharmarāja was there together with Kṛṣṇā.

sanskrit: sa praveśāya cāśakto gamanāya ca pāṇḍavaḥ tasya cārtasya tair vākyaiś codyamānaḥ punaḥ punaḥ ākrande tatra kaunteyaś cintayām āsa duḥkhitaḥ
english: Unable to enter and unable to go away, the Pāṇḍava was urged again and again by the brahmin's words of distress. There, amid that outcry, the son of Kuntī pondered, filled with grief.

sanskrit: hriyamāṇe dhane tasmin brāhmaṇasya tapasvinaḥ aśrupramārjanaṃ tasya kartavyam iti niścitaḥ
english: "As the wealth of that ascetic brahmin is being carried away, it is my duty to wipe away his tears" — so he resolved.

sanskrit: upaprekṣaṇajo 'dharmaḥ sumahān syān mahīpateḥ yady asya rudato dvāri na karomy adya rakṣaṇam
english: "The sin of negligent inaction would be very great for a ruler of the earth if today I do not protect this weeping man at my very door."

sanskrit: anāstikyaṃ ca sarveṣām asmākam api rakṣaṇe pratitiṣṭheta loke 'sminn adharmaś caiva no bhavet
english: "And disbelief in all of us would become established in this world if we fail to protect, and unrighteousness would also be ours."

sanskrit: anāpṛcchya ca rājānaṃ gate mayi na saṃśayaḥ ajātaśatror nṛpater mama caivāpriyaṃ bhavet
english: "And if I go without asking the king, without doubt it will displease King Ajātaśatru as well as me."

sanskrit: anupraveśe rājñas tu vanavāso bhaven mama adharmo vā mahān astu vane vā maraṇaṃ mama śarīrasyāpi nāśena dharma eva viśiṣyate
english: "But if I enter the king's chamber, I shall have to go to the forest. Let there be great unrighteousness, or let me die in the forest — even at the cost of my body's destruction, dharma alone prevails."

sanskrit: evaṃ viniścitya tataḥ kuntīputro dhanaṃjayaḥ anupraviśya rājānam āpṛcchya ca viśāṃ pate
english: Having thus resolved, Dhanañjaya son of Kuntī entered, took leave of the king, O lord of the people,

sanskrit: dhanur ādāya saṃhṛṣṭo brāhmaṇaṃ pratyabhāṣata brāhmaṇāgamyatāṃ śīghraṃ yāvat paradhanaiṣiṇaḥ
english: and, taking up his bow with joy, spoke to the brahmin: "Come quickly, O brahmin, while those who seek another's wealth still have not gone far."

sanskrit: na dūre te gatāḥ kṣudrās tāvad gacchāmahe saha yāvad āvartayāmy adya corahastād dhanaṃ tava
english: "Those wretches have not gone far — let us go together now, so that today I may recover your wealth from the hands of the thieves."

sanskrit: so 'nusṛtya mahābāhur dhanvī varmī rathī dhvajī śarair vidhvaṃsitāṃś corān avajitya ca tad dhanam
english: The mighty-armed one, bearing his bow, armored, mounted on his chariot with his banner, pursued them, scattered the thieves with his arrows, and conquered that wealth.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇasya upāhṛtya yaśaḥ pītvā ca pāṇḍavaḥ ājagāma puraṃ vīraḥ savyasācī paraṃtapaḥ
english: Having restored it to the brahmin and having drunk deep of glory, the heroic Pāṇḍava Savyasācī, scorcher of foes, returned to the city.

sanskrit: so 'bhivādya gurūn sarvāṃs taiś cāpi pratinanditaḥ dharmarājam uvācedaṃ vratam ādiśyatāṃ mama
english: He saluted all the elders, and being greeted by them in return, he said to Dharmarāja: "Let the vow be prescribed for me."

sanskrit: samayaḥ samatikrānto bhavatsaṃdarśanān mayā vanavāsaṃ gamiṣyāmi samayo hy eṣa naḥ kṛtaḥ
english: "The compact has been transgressed by me by my coming into your presence; I shall go to the forest, for this is the agreement we made."

sanskrit: ity ukto dharmarājas tu sahasā vākyam apriyam katham ity abravīd vācā śokārtaḥ sajjamānayā yudhiṣṭhiro guḍākeśaṃ bhrātā bhrātaram acyutam
english: When thus addressed, Dharmarāja was suddenly struck by this unwelcome word; and Yudhiṣṭhira, grieved and with faltering speech, said "How so?" to Guḍākeśa — one brother to the other, the steadfast one.

sanskrit: pramāṇam asmi yadi te mattaḥ śṛṇu vaco 'nagha anupraveśe yad vīra kṛtavāṃs tvaṃ mamāpriyam sarvaṃ tad anujānāmi vyalīkaṃ na ca me hṛdi
english: "If I am an authority for you, hear my word, O sinless one. Whatever displeasure you caused me, O hero, by entering — I pardon all of it; it is not a grievance in my heart."

sanskrit: guror anupraveśo hi nopaghāto yavīyasaḥ yavīyaso 'nupraveśo jyeṣṭhasya vidhilopakaḥ
english: "For a younger brother's entry into the elder's presence is no offence; it is the younger one's entry that violates the rule for the eldest."

sanskrit: nivartasva mahābāho kuruṣva vacanaṃ mama na hi te dharmalopo 'sti na ca me dharṣaṇā kṛtā
english: "Turn back, O mighty-armed one, and obey my word; there is no breach of dharma for you, nor has any offence been done to me."

sanskrit: arjuna uvāca na vyājena cared dharmam iti me bhavataḥ śrutam na satyād vicaliṣyāmi satyenāyudham ālabhe
english: Arjuna said: "I have heard from you that one should not practise dharma under a pretext. I will not swerve from truth — by truth I take up my weapon."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca so 'bhyanujñāpya rājānaṃ brahmacaryāya dīkṣitaḥ vane dvādaśa varṣāṇi vāsāyopajagāma ha
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having obtained the king's permission, he was initiated into the vow of celibacy and came to dwell in the forest for twelve years.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca taṃ prayāntaṃ mahābāhuṃ kauravāṇāṃ yaśaskaram anujagmur mahātmāno brāhmaṇā vedapāragāḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: As the mighty-armed glory of the Kauravas set out, great-souled brahmins who had mastered the Vedas followed him.

sanskrit: vedavedāṅgavidvāṃsas tathaivādhyātmacintakāḥ caukṣāś ca bhagavadbhaktāḥ sūtāḥ paurāṇikāś ca ye
english: Those learned in the Vedas and their ancillaries, as well as thinkers on the self, the pure and those devoted to the Lord, bards and those versed in the Purāṇas,

sanskrit: kathakāś cāpare rājañ śramaṇāś ca vanaukasaḥ divyākhyānāni ye cāpi paṭhanti madhuraṃ dvijāḥ
english: other storytellers, O king, ascetic forest-dwellers, and brahmins who sweetly recite celestial narratives —

sanskrit: etaiś cānyaiś ca bahubhiḥ sahāyaiḥ pāṇḍunandanaḥ vṛtaḥ ślakṣṇakathaiḥ prāyān marudbhir iva vāsavaḥ
english: by these and many other companions with pleasing speech, the son of Pāṇḍu was surrounded and proceeded like Vāsava amid the Maruts.

sanskrit: ramaṇīyāni citrāṇi vanāni ca sarāṃsi ca saritaḥ sāgarāṃś caiva deśān api ca bhārata
english: Pleasant and varied forests, lakes, rivers, oceans, and regions too, O Bhārata,

sanskrit: puṇyāni caiva tīrthāni dadarśa bharatarṣabha sa gaṅgādvāram āsādya niveśam akarot prabhuḥ
english: and holy pilgrimage sites he saw, O bull of the Bhāratas; reaching Gaṅgādvāra, the lord set up his camp.

sanskrit: tatra tasyādbhutaṃ karma śṛṇu me janamejaya kṛtavān yad viśuddhātmā pāṇḍūnāṃ pravaro rathī
english: Hear from me, O Janamejaya, the wonderful deed that the pure-souled foremost charioteer of the Pāṇḍus performed there.

sanskrit: niviṣṭe tatra kaunteye brāhmaṇeṣu ca bhārata agnihotrāṇi viprās te prāduścakrur anekaśaḥ
english: When the son of Kuntī had settled there, O Bhārata, those brahmins kindled their sacred fires many times over.

sanskrit: teṣu prabodhyamāneṣu jvaliteṣu huteṣu ca kṛtapuṣpopahāreṣu tīrāntaragateṣu ca
english: While those fires were being kindled, blazing, and fed with oblations, flower-offerings having been made, the brahmins having gone to the bank of the ford,

sanskrit: kṛtābhiṣekair vidvadbhir niyataiḥ satpathi sthitaiḥ śuśubhe 'tīva tad rājan gaṅgādvāraṃ mahātmabhiḥ
english: with the learned ones having bathed, disciplined and established on the good path — that Gaṅgādvāra shone exceedingly, O king, with those great souls.

sanskrit: tathā paryākule tasmin niveśe pāṇḍunandanaḥ abhiṣekāya kaunteyo gaṅgām avatatāra ha
english: As that encampment was thus filled with activity, the son of Pāṇḍu, the son of Kuntī, descended into the Gaṅgā for his ritual bath.

sanskrit: tatrābhiṣekaṃ kṛtvā sa tarpayitvā pitāmahān uttitīrṣur jalād rājann agnikāryacikīrṣayā
english: Having bathed there and satisfied the ancestors, and wishing to ascend from the water in order to perform the fire-rite, O king,

sanskrit: apakṛṣṭo mahābāhur nāgarājasya kanyayā antarjale mahārāja ulūpyā kāmayānayā
english: the mighty-armed one was drawn beneath the water, O great king, by Ulūpī, the daughter of the serpent king, who was overcome with desire.

sanskrit: dadarśa pāṇḍavas tatra pāvakaṃ susamāhitam kauravyasyātha nāgasya bhavane paramārcite
english: There the Pāṇḍava beheld fire burning clearly and well-tended in the highly honored dwelling of that serpent of the Kauravya line.

sanskrit: tatrāgnikāryaṃ kṛtavān kuntīputro dhanaṃjayaḥ aśaṅkamānena hutas tenātuṣyad dhutāśanaḥ
english: There Dhanañjaya, son of Kuntī, performed his fire-rite; offered without hesitation, the fire was pleased with him.

sanskrit: agnikāryaṃ sa kṛtvā tu nāgarājasutāṃ tadā prahasann iva kaunteya idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Having performed the fire-rite, the son of Kuntī then spoke this word to the daughter of the serpent king, smiling as it were:

sanskrit: kim idaṃ sāhasaṃ bhīru kṛtavaty asi bhāmini kaś cāyaṃ subhago deśaḥ kā ca tvaṃ kasya cātmajā
english: "What is this bold deed you have done, O timid one, O beautiful lady? What is this charming place? And who are you, whose daughter?"

sanskrit: ulūpy uvāca airāvatakule jātaḥ kauravyo nāma pannagaḥ tasyāsmi duhitā pārtha ulūpī nāma pannagī
english: Ulūpī said: "A serpent born in the Airāvata lineage, named Kauravya — I am his daughter, O Pārtha; I am the serpent maiden named Ulūpī."

sanskrit: sāhaṃ tvām abhiṣekārtham avatīrṇaṃ samudragām dṛṣṭavaty eva kaunteya kandarpeṇāsmi mūrcchitā
english: "When I saw you, O son of Kuntī, descending into the river for your bath, I was at once overcome by Kandarpа, the god of love."

sanskrit: tāṃ mām anaṅgamathitāṃ tvatkṛte kurunandana ananyāṃ tvām upagataṃ nandayasvādya pradānenātmano rahaḥ
english: "Me, thus tormented by the bodiless one on your account, O joy of the Kurus — I who have come to you and to no other — gladden today by giving yourself to me in private."

sanskrit: arjuna uvāca brahmacaryam idaṃ bhadre mama dvādaśavārṣikam dharmarājena cādiṣṭaṃ nāham asmi svayaṃvaśaḥ
english: Arjuna said: "This twelve-year vow of celibacy has been enjoined upon me by Dharmarāja; I am not my own master, O fortunate one."

sanskrit: tava cāpi priyaṃ kartum icchāmi jalacāriṇi anṛtaṃ noktapūrvaṃ ca mayā kiṃ cana karhi cit
english: "And I wish to do what is pleasing to you as well, O dweller in the water; I have never spoken an untruth at any time."

sanskrit: kathaṃ ca nānṛtaṃ tat syāt tava cāpi priyaṃ bhavet na ca pīḍyeta me dharmas tathā kuryāṃ bhujaṃgame
english: "How then might that not be untruth and yet what is pleasing to you might also come about, and my dharma might not be harmed — tell me how to act so, O serpent maiden."

sanskrit: ulūpy uvāca jānāmy ahaṃ pāṇḍaveya yathā carasi medinīm yathā ca te brahmacaryam idam ādiṣṭavān guruḥ
english: Ulūpī said: "I know, O son of Pāṇḍu, how you wander the earth, and how your preceptor enjoined this celibacy upon you."

sanskrit: parasparaṃ vartamānān drupadasyātmajāṃ prati yo no 'nupraviśen mohāt sa no dvādaśavārṣikam vane cared brahmacaryam iti vaḥ samayaḥ kṛtaḥ
english: "Whichever of you, heedlessly, were to intrude upon the other in the presence of Drupada's daughter — he was to observe celibacy in the forest for twelve years: this is the compact you made."

sanskrit: tad idaṃ draupadīhetor anyonyasya pravāsanam kṛtaṃ vas tatra dharmārtham atra dharmo na duṣyati
english: "This exile from one another was made for the sake of Draupadī, for the purpose of dharma — in this matter dharma is not violated."

sanskrit: paritrāṇaṃ ca kartavyam ārtānāṃ pṛthulocana kṛtvā mama paritrāṇaṃ tava dharmo na lupyate
english: "And the rescue of those in distress is a duty, O large-eyed one; by rescuing me, your dharma is not diminished."

sanskrit: yadi vāpy asya dharmasya sūkṣmo 'pi syād vyatikramaḥ sa ca te dharma eva syād dāttvā prāṇān mamārjuna
english: "And even if there were the slightest transgression of this dharma, that too would be dharma for you — by giving me life, O Arjuna."

sanskrit: bhaktāṃ bhajasva māṃ pārtha satām etan mataṃ prabho na kariṣyasi ced evaṃ mṛtāṃ mām upadhāraya
english: "Cherish me who am devoted to you, O Pārtha; this is the view of the good, O lord. If you do not act thus, know me as dead."

sanskrit: prāṇadānān mahābāho cara dharmam anuttamam śaraṇaṃ ca prapannāsmi tvām adya puruṣottama
english: "By the gift of life practise the highest dharma, O mighty-armed one; I have come to you for refuge today, O best of men."

sanskrit: dīnān anāthān kaunteya parirakṣasi nityaśaḥ sāhaṃ śaraṇam abhyemi roravīmi ca duḥkhitā
english: "O son of Kuntī, you always protect the wretched and the unprotected; I come to you for shelter and I cry out in grief."

sanskrit: yāce tvām abhikāmāhaṃ tasmāt kuru mama priyam sa tvam ātmapradānena sakāmāṃ kartum arhasi
english: "I beg you, being desirous of you; therefore do what is pleasing to me. You — you are the one who should fulfil my desire by giving yourself."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evam uktas tu kaunteyaḥ pannageśvarakanyayā kṛtavāṃs tat tathā sarvaṃ dharmam uddiśya kāraṇam
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Thus addressed by the daughter of the serpent king, the son of Kuntī did all of that, citing dharma as the reason.

sanskrit: sa nāgabhavane rātriṃ tām uṣitvā pratāpavān udite 'bhyutthitaḥ sūrye kauravyasya niveśanāt
english: That valiant one, having spent that night in the serpent's dwelling, rose at sunrise and departed from the abode of Kauravya.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca kathayitvā tu tat sarvaṃ brāhmaṇebhyaḥ sa bhārata prayayau himavatpārśvaṃ tato vajradharātmajaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having narrated all that to the brahmins, O Bhārata, the son of the wielder of the thunderbolt then journeyed to the slopes of the Himālaya.

sanskrit: agastyavaṭam āsādya vasiṣṭhasya ca parvatam bhṛgutuṅge ca kaunteyaḥ kṛtavāñ śaucam ātmanaḥ
english: Reaching the Agastya-banyan tree, the mountain of Vasiṣṭha, and the heights of Bhṛgu, the son of Kuntī performed his purification.

sanskrit: pradadau gosahasrāṇi tīrtheṣv āyataneṣu ca niveśāṃś ca dvijātibhyaḥ so 'dadat kurusattamaḥ
english: He gave thousands of cattle and also dwellings to the twice-born at the sacred fords and shrines — that best of Kurus gave.

sanskrit: hiraṇyabindos tīrthe ca snātvā puruṣasattamaḥ dṛṣṭavān parvataśreṣṭhaṃ puṇyāny āyatanāni ca
english: And bathing at the ford of Hiraṇyabindu, that best of men beheld the finest mountains and the sacred shrines.

sanskrit: avatīrya naraśreṣṭho brāhmaṇaiḥ saha bhārata prācīṃ diśam abhiprepsur jagāma bharatarṣabhaḥ
english: Descending with the brahmins, O Bhārata, that best of men, bull of the Bhāratas, set out with the intention of reaching the eastern direction.

sanskrit: ānupūrvyeṇa tīrthāni dṛṣṭavān kurusattamaḥ nadīṃ cotpalinīṃ ramyām araṇyaṃ naimiṣaṃ prati
english: The best of Kurus visited the pilgrimage sites in due order, and the lovely river Utpalinī, towards the Naimiṣa forest.

sanskrit: nandām aparanandāṃ ca kauśikīṃ ca yaśasvinīm mahānadīṃ gayāṃ caiva gaṅgām api ca bhārata
english: The Nandā, the Aparanandā, the celebrated Kauśikī, the great river, Gayā, and the Gaṅgā as well, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: evaṃ sarvāṇi tīrthāni paśyamānas tathāśramān ātmanaḥ pāvanaṃ kurvan brāhmaṇebhyo dadau vasu
english: Thus beholding all the pilgrimage sites and hermitages, purifying himself, he gave wealth to the brahmins.

sanskrit: aṅgavaṅgakaliṅgeṣu yāni puṇyāni kāni cit jagāma tāni sarvāṇi tīrthāny āyatanāni ca dṛṣṭvā ca vidhivat tāni dhanaṃ cāpi dadau tataḥ
english: Whatever sacred sites and shrines existed in Aṅga, Vaṅga, and Kaliṅga — he went to all of them, and having duly visited them, he gave wealth there as well.

sanskrit: kaliṅgarāṣṭradvāreṣu brāhmaṇāḥ pāṇḍavānugāḥ abhyanujñāya kaunteyam upāvartanta bhārata
english: At the borders of the Kaliṅga kingdom, the brahmins who had been accompanying the Pāṇḍava took leave of the son of Kuntī and turned back, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: sa tu tair abhyanujñātaḥ kuntīputro dhanaṃjayaḥ sahāyair alpakaiḥ śūraḥ prayayau yena sāgaram
english: Bidden farewell by them, that hero Dhanañjaya son of Kuntī, with few companions, set out in the direction of the ocean.

sanskrit: sa kaliṅgān atikramya deśān āyatanāni ca dharmyāṇi ramaṇīyāni prekṣamāṇo yayau prabhuḥ
english: Crossing through Kaliṅga and beholding the righteous and lovely lands and shrines, the lord journeyed on.

sanskrit: mahendraparvataṃ dṛṣṭvā tāpasair upaśobhitam samudratīreṇa śanair maṇalūraṃ jagāma ha
english: Having seen the Mahendra mountain adorned with ascetics, he slowly went along the seashore to Maṇalūra.

sanskrit: tatra sarvāṇi tīrthāni puṇyāny āyatanāni ca abhigamya mahābāhur abhyagacchan mahīpatim maṇalūreśvaraṃ rājan dharmajñaṃ citravāhanam
english: Having visited all the sacred fords and shrines there, the mighty-armed one approached the lord of the earth, O king — the ruler of Maṇalūra, Citravāhana, knower of dharma.

sanskrit: tasya citrāṅgadā nāma duhitā cārudarśanā tāṃ dadarśa pure tasmin vicarantīṃ yadṛcchayā
english: That king had a daughter named Citrāṅgadā, beautiful to behold; Arjuna saw her wandering at will in that city.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā ca tāṃ varārohāṃ cakame caitravāhinīm abhigamya ca rājānaṃ jñāpayat svaṃ prayojanam tam uvācātha rājā sa sāntvapūrvam idaṃ vacaḥ
english: Seeing that woman of noble bearing, he desired Citravāhinī; and approaching the king, he made known his intention. The king then spoke these words to him with conciliation:
